findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done — In new repos and repos upgraded to v1.2.51, close gets a valid Neon review report using the supplied diff, evidence, and read-only file tools even after a shell command is denied.
Case: normal use - A shell permission request contains only its tool-call ID, with no preceding notification identifying the tool. `shell_refused` remains false, so line 539 skips the follow-up and close repeats the original review instead of recovering. This request form is modeled by `tests/stubs/agy:114` and was explicitly covered in an earlier fix at `.factory/fixes/neon-s-review-ends-with-review-engine-re.json:152`. The [ACP contract](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/tool-calls) permits an ID-only permission update and recommends, rather than requires, the preceding tool-call notification.
findings.title: Not done: Close cannot recover from an ID-only shell denial

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test — In new repos and repos upgraded to v1.2.51, close gets a valid Neon review report using the supplied diff, evidence, and read-only file tools even after a shell command is denied.
Case: normal use - The named proof covers only `request` and `update`, both preceded by a tool-call notification identifying the shell command. It still passes while the ID-only request modeled by `tests/stubs/agy:114` bypasses recovery in `src/forge/antigravity.py:412`. The end-to-end proof needs to exercise that request and verify that close receives the completed report.
findings.title: Test: Close gets a valid Neon review after a denied shell command

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - The first review turn returns token usage, but the follow-up receives a rate-limit or connection error. `ask()` raises before `ran.update(tokens)` at line 555, so the `review_engine` cleanup at lines 232–246 writes an empty usage object. `src/forge/time_records.py:578` then excludes the known first-turn usage from review totals, losing the accounting for a billed run.
findings.title: Preserve the first turn's usage when the follow-up fails

why: When Neon tries to run a shell command and ends its turn without a report, Forge repeats the review with the same instructions and close stays blocked.
